# Sequence Integration After Unit Testing

**Decision.** Re-link *integration testing* to start **after** *unit testing* with a Finish-to-Start
dependency, instead of running the two in parallel, to clear an over-allocation of the Backend
Developer. Accept the resulting slip rather than compress or resource around it.

**Date.** Recorded in lab 5–6 of [[computer-project-management]], committed 2026-07-10.

## Why

The conflict is a resourcing problem; the fix is a scheduling one.

> "an **over-allocation of the Backend Developer** was fixed by re-linking
> *integration testing* to start **after** *unit testing* (FS) instead of in parallel. The"
> — Computer Project Management/lab5-6_Baseline_and_Tracking/README.md, 2026-07-10

Combined with four task extensions — most importantly unit testing at **+16 days** for real test
coverage — the cascade moved the finish from the baseline's 24 Aug to 8 Sep:

> "| Duration | 123 d | 134 d | **+11 d** |"
> — Computer Project Management/lab5-6_Baseline_and_Tracking/README.md, 2026-07-10

Sixteen days of extension producing eleven days of slip is float being consumed; the residue
propagates because the newly-serialised pair now sits on the [[critical-path-method|critical path]],
which from the reporting date runs *integration testing → UAT → deployment → documentation →
closure*. See [[schedule-baseline-and-variance]] for the full delta.

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not, per the repo |
|---|---|
| **Keep both tests in parallel** | the incumbent — leaves the Backend Developer double-booked, i.e. a plan that cannot execute |
| **Add a second Backend Developer** | not taken. The repo's own seminar argues against it: Brooks' Law, slide 11 — see [[project-environment-factors]] |
| **Crash or fast-track the chain** | never costed in any readable file |
| **Automatic leveling instead of a manual re-link** | leveling was used one lab earlier ([[resource-leveling]]); here the conflict is resolved by hand, as a dependency edit |

The second row is the interesting one. The same repository contains both the resource conflict and
the argument for why throwing a person at it would not have helped — in two artefacts that never
cross-reference each other.

## The defensible part, technically

Serialising unit before integration is not merely a scheduling convenience: integration testing
against components that have not passed their own unit tests produces failures whose cause is
ambiguous. The FS link buys diagnostic clarity as well as an unbooked resource.
